$comment: Where a quoted span is in a text, as every implementation must answer it. A model asked to mark a text quotes it: the words (`exact`), and maybe some of what comes before and after them (`prefix`, `suffix`). None of that is trusted. It is reconciled against the text into a position and a quote that are the text's own, or it is refused, and only what is reconciled is built into an annotation. TypeScript (packages/core: reconcileSelector) runs every case and fails on a difference; a worker written in another language runs the same file. READING A CASE. `text` is the real text, `quoted` what the model said, and `reconciled` the answer: `null` when the span is refused, otherwise `start` and `end` (the span is the characters from `start` up to but not including `end`), `exact` (the text between them, never the model's spelling of it), `prefix` and `suffix` (taken from the text as CONTEXT says, each left out when there is nothing to take), `anchorMethod` (how the place was found) and, only when that is `fuzzy-match`, `matchQuality` (which of the three looser searches found it). THE RULE. An empty `exact` is refused. Otherwise find every place the text has `exact`, character for character; places may overlap one another. Exactly one place: it is the span, `unique-match`, whatever the model's prefix and suffix say. More than one: a prefix or a suffix the model gave is a hint, and an empty one is none. If there is a hint, the span is the first place, in the text's order, that fits every hint given, `context-recovered`. A place fits the prefix when the text just before it ends with the prefix, or when the prefix, with the white space at its two ends removed, is anywhere in the characters before the place: as many of them as the prefix is long, and at least 32. It fits the suffix when the text just after it starts with the suffix, or when the suffix, trimmed the same way, is anywhere in the characters after the place: as many as the suffix is long, and at least 32. With no hint, or no place that fits, the span is the first place, `first-of-many`. No place at all: three looser searches are tried in this order, the hints playing no part, and the first that finds a span answers `fuzzy-match` with its own name as `matchQuality`. (1) `normalized`. Normalize the text and `exact` alike: every run of white space becomes one space, the single quotation marks U+2018 and U+2019 become an apostrophe, the double ones U+201C and U+201D become a straight double quote, an em dash U+2014 becomes two hyphens and an en dash U+2013 one, and white space at the two ends is dropped. Take the first place the normalized text has the normalized `exact`. The span starts at the character of the text that the first matched character came from, and ends at the character that the one after the match came from, a run of white space counting as its first character; when nothing comes after the match, it ends just after the last character of the text that is not white space. (2) `case-insensitive`. Lower-case the text and `exact` by Unicode's own rule, of no particular language, and take the first place the one has the other; the span starts there and is as long as `exact`. (3) `fuzzy`. Compare `exact` with every stretch of the text that has as many characters as it has, by edit distance: the least number of single characters inserted, deleted or replaced that turns one into the other. The span is the stretch at the least distance, the first of them if several share it, provided that distance is within the allowance: a twentieth of the length of `exact`, rounded down, and never less than 5. If no stretch is within it, or the text is shorter than `exact`, the span is refused. CONTEXT. The `prefix` is the 64 characters of the text before the span, or all of them if there are fewer. If it would begin part of the way through a word it is lengthened backwards a character at a time, by at most 32 more, until the character before it is a boundary or the text begins. The `suffix` is the 64 characters after the span, or all there are, lengthened forwards in the same way until the character after it is a boundary or the text ends. A boundary is white space or one of these eighteen and nothing else: . , ; : ! ? ' " ( ) [ ] { } < > / \ (so not a hyphen, and not a curly quotation mark). White space is what Unicode gives the White_Space property; no case rests on U+0085 or U+FEFF, about which implementations disagree. Characters are compared as they are, with no Unicode normalization: a letter followed by a combining mark is not the one accented letter. What an offset counts is stated in a table of its own; every text here is of the Basic Multilingual Plane, where it makes no difference. `defects` says what today's rule does that is a mistake: no case states any of it, and an implementation is not held to it. Add a case here before changing an implementation.
defects: The allowance of the `fuzzy` search is never less than 5, however short `exact` is. For an `exact` of five characters or fewer every stretch of its length is within the allowance, so one that is nowhere in the text is anchored to the nearest stretch of that length instead of being refused.
The `fuzzy` search looks only at stretches exactly as long as `exact`. An `exact` that has dropped or added a character is anchored to a span that is a character out at one end.

The `case-insensitive` search finds a position in the lower-cased text and uses it as a position in the text. Where lower-casing changes how many characters come before the match (U+0130, a capital I with a dot, becomes two) the span is displaced.
A `normalized` match with nothing after it ends its span at the very end of the text, not after the last character that is not white space: white space the text ends with is taken into `exact`.
A hint that is only white space is trimmed to nothing, and nothing is found everywhere: the first place is answered as `context-recovered` though no context recovered it.
An `exact` that is only white space and is not in the text normalizes to nothing, which is found at the start of the normalized text: the answer is an empty span, not a refusal.

The hints are not consulted once `exact` is not in the text character for character: of several places a looser search could take, it takes the first, even when a prefix or a suffix says which was meant.
